source.title: Revisiting associative recall in modern recurrent models

page_placements.theme: Loss bumps and abrupt ICL gains without induction heads
Architectural changes that build in or reroute induction (KV shifting, convolution, n-gram heads, value residuals)

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures associative-recall performance and training-loss dynamics in trained models, but does not directly identify or intervene on induction-head circuits.
record.gate_note: The paper analyzes one-layer training dynamics and MQAR recall, but does not directly probe induction heads or measure loss by token index. Its proposed interpretation that a one-layer Attention model attempts to form induction heads is explicitly a hypothesis. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study never identifies, probes or ablates attention heads, and never measures in-context learning as loss by token index. It reports MQAR accuracy and loss curves, and it labels the one-layer Attention loss bump an 'attempt to form induction heads' as an explicit hypothesis. Its results are about associative-recall capability and optimization stability, which are related to but different from the induction-head claim. No version is tested, so the findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The central conclusion is that SSMs differ from Transformers mainly in optimization stability: success is confined to a narrow learning-rate window, and SSMs favour width while Transformers favour depth. On induction heads, the authors report that one-layer Attention shows a loss bump resembling the induction-head phenomenon without accuracy gains, and they hypothesize a failed attempt at induction-head formation. Mamba shows a similar bump but solves the task, while Hyena is smooth. They state that SSM recall dynamics 'do not resemble the formation of induction heads'.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains small models on synthetic MQAR and measures task performance and training dynamics; it does not reproduce the original induction-head circuit analysis or token-index ICL measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate strongly affects recurrent-model task performance; recurrent models have a narrow successful learning-rate window, unlike the broader robustness reported for Attention. The study also varies architecture and width/depth.

fits_no_version.finding: One-layer Attention shows a sudden test-loss bump while MQAR accuracy stays flat (about 2%). The authors hypothesize this is a failed attempt at induction-head formation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A loss bump resembling the induction-head phase change can occur in a one-layer Transformer without any gain in recall accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: One-layer Attention fails MQAR (2%) but reaches 99% with a 1D convolution on QKV, K or V. Convolution on Q alone stays at 2%. Two-layer Attention solves the task in all settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Associative recall in attention needs either a second layer or local token mixing on keys or values (consistent with, but not a test of, previous-token composition).

fits_no_version.finding: One-layer Mamba also shows a significant loss bump yet solves MQAR with a tuned learning rate. Hyena's training dynamics are smooth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss bumps in training are not specific to Transformer induction-head formation.

record.code_released: The authors state that all code is publicly available; URL not stated.
record.problems: Induction-head formation is inferred rather than directly measured. Training dynamics are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The experiments use synthetic benchmarks, and the authors note that validation on downstream language-modeling tasks remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for unrelated copying-task, learning-rate sweep, or other recurrent-model accuracy results; those do not measure induction-head formation or the specified token-index ICL measure. Cited results from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Head identification, previous-token-head composition and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] circuit; only recall accuracy is reported.
Timing of head formation and its co-occurrence with an ICL gain measured by token-index loss; the one-layer bump is not linked to measured heads.
Not addressed; there are no large models and no token-index ICL measure.
Not addressed; heads with induction behaviour are never sought in Mamba or other architectures.
The learning-rate and width/depth effects concern recall accuracy, not induction-head formation.

record.verdict_notes: Downgraded from 'tests'/T2 to 'discusses'/T6: induction heads are an interpretive frame only, and no row measures heads or token-index ICL. The reader's V1 'supports' and V2 'limits_scope' labels were removed. The study also reports that more than two Attention layers give no further MQAR gain, and that one-layer Attention width has no effect, recalling on average about one key-value pair. Neither bears on a version.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests MQAR recall performance in Attention models, including a two-layer model, but does not identify heads, test previous-token-head composition, or directly establish the [A][B] … [A] → [B] circuit.

The study reports training-loss dynamics and MQAR accuracy for one-layer models, but does not track induction-head formation or measure in-context learning as later-token loss falling relative to earlier-token loss.
Learning-rate sensitivity is reported for model task performance, but the study does not test whether induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning depends on data or training setup.
The study does not test whether induction-head formation comprises distinct sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

relation.reason: The study discusses induction-head circuits and interprets a loss bump by analogy, without testing or using an identified circuit.

tranche.reason: The study measures synthetic recall capability and optimization dynamics. Induction-head formation is hypothesized from loss dynamics; neither heads nor token-index in-context learning are measured.

source_check.notes: Section 6 and the conclusion report a Mamba loss bump, whereas Figure 6's caption describes both recurrent models as smooth. The approximately 2% Attention accuracy comes from Tables 2–3; Section 6 states that accuracy remains largely unchanged.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Two-layer Attention solves the associative-recall task, supporting the task-behavior component only; R1. The circuit mechanism remains untested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: A sudden test-loss bump was not accompanied by an MQAR-accuracy increase; this limits the inference from a loss bump alone, although MQAR accuracy is not the specified token-index ICL measure; R2-R3.
